teams.heading: Chairman says Jake White will not boot Fiji's flair into touch
teams.body: Fiji's chairman says Jake White will not coach the flair out of the side as the team chases a place at next year's World Cup in Australia. The stance echoes what White has said since his 34-28 win over Japan in Tokyo, when he spoke of wanting "a little bit of control" without losing the flair. White, who picked no Europe-based players for that game, believes the squad can be "a massive force" in Australia, and Fiji face France, Ireland and Italy in November.

lead.why: The Japan result and the Nawaqanitawase and squad stories have already run, and this is the only remaining Fiji item with a clear headline.

teams.heading: England scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet signs new Leicester Tigers contract
teams.body: England scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet has committed his future to Leicester Tigers with a new deal, confirming his place as the club vice-captain. The 25-year-old, who came through the Tigers academy and has 118 appearances for the club, said: "It was a pretty easy decision to stay." Planet Rugby lists him among the scrum-halves ahead of Harry Randall in the pecking order for England's November squad, and he has 27 caps. He has also earned an 'Elite Player Squad' contract for 2026-27.

lead.why: The only new England-player item not already run today, and it concerns a 27-cap scrum-half's future.

teams.heading: Billy Searle rejected a France return to push on at Leicester Tigers
teams.body: Leicester fly-half Billy Searle turned down a potential return to France to "push his game on" at Welford Road, the 30-year-old told BBC Radio Leicester. Searle, who has also played in France for Toulouse, Biarritz and Agen, signed a new three-year deal with the club in September. He has also not given up hope of adding a first senior cap to his England A appearance against Ireland, which would not have been possible had he moved back to France.

teams.heading: Stuart McCloskey crosses for Ulster in 34-26 defeat to Bulls
teams.body: Stuart McCloskey bundled over for a try that brought Ulster within striking distance of the Bulls, after assisting an earlier score in the 34-26 URC defeat at Loftus Versfeld. Planet Rugby rated the performance an 8 and called it a "statement performance" that will put Andy Farrell on notice just before the Nations Championship. He also held Johan Grobbelaar up over the line with Tom Stewart in the 11th minute.

teams.heading: Italy remain winless in three games, 11th of 12 in the log
teams.body: Italy sit 11th of 12 in the log after three matches, and all three have been lost. Across those games they have scored 37 points and conceded 131, a points difference of -94. Their most recent outing was a 10-57 defeat to Australia in Round 3, and the next assignment is Round 4 against South Africa, the side that beat them 32-14 at home in November 2025.

teams.heading: Tom English wants Kyle Rowe in Scotland's Nations Championship mix
teams.body: Tom English, answering readers' questions for BBC Sport, says Kyle Rowe is an inch away from Scotland's wing spots and would want him in the mix. Dobie and Steyn are his most consistent wings right now, and he sees logic in Dobie covering two positions from the bench, with Rowe and Steyn starting. That would leave Darcy Graham out of the 23, which English calls a hard call.

teams.heading: Uncapped Macs Page forced off with head injury against Stormers
teams.body: Uncapped Scarlets wing Macs Page was forced off in concerning scenes during the URC clash with the Stormers in Cape Town. The 21-year-old, who had already scored his fifth try of the season, seemingly lost consciousness after his head hit the turf while being tackled short of the line, and walked off on oxygen. He narrowly missed out on Steve Tandy's 39-man autumn squad, and Scarlets director of rugby Nigel Davies says a Wales call-up is a matter of when, not if. No coverage of his condition is in today's press.

teams.heading: Sam Prendergast's fitness for Argentina clash still unconfirmed in latest coverage
teams.body: Ireland's Sam Prendergast remains unconfirmed for the November clash with Argentina, and today's coverage adds no new update. RTÉ Sport reported him as a doubt with a wrist injury, and a Sun report called it a major injury scare, but neither has been followed by a confirmed ruling. Argentina, meanwhile, take a 33-man roster into a London camp from Monday, with Felipe Contepomi naming his November squad once it finishes.

teams.heading: Wallabies flanker Rob Leota signs with Clermont after leaving Bayonne
teams.body: Rob Leota has joined Clermont from Bayonne, committing to the club until January 2027. The 29-year-old, who has 21 caps for Australia, was a free agent since leaving Bayonne, and Clermont are waiting on several injured players to return. Coach Christophe Urios is looking for a powerful ball carrier who can contribute quickly. Leota is not among the 33 players Les Kiss named for the spring tour.

lead.why: It is the only NEW item on the shortlist, and the Test-squad stories have already been run.

teams.heading: Japan's last 11 games have averaged 29.7 points scored per match
teams.body: In their last 11 games, Japan have scored 327 points, an average of 29.7 a game. Over the same window they have conceded 301, or 27.4 a game. Their biggest win in that run was a 63-14 home victory over USA in September's Pacific Nations Cup knockout stage. Put together, the two totals come to 628 points in 11 games.

teams.heading: Richie Mo'unga not yet ruled out of Europe tour after calf tear
teams.body: Richie Mo'unga has not yet been ruled out of the Nations Championship tour, the one faint positive in a long list of All Blacks absences. The flyhalf missed both Bledisloe Cup Tests with a calf tear, and the coverage gives no timeline for his return. Scotland, England and Wales are still on the itinerary before the finals weekend at Twickenham, and Mo'unga's name is absent from the players already ruled out. Whether he is available for those matches remains open.

teams.heading: Planet Rugby dissects South Africa's eight Test defeats since 2023
teams.body: Planet Rugby has gone through South Africa's eight Test defeats since the start of 2023 and concludes they read like a coaching manual for beating the Springboks. Its checklist: survive the set piece, attack before the defence resets, keep possession tight, and take the points on offer. The timing matters: Italy, France and Ireland await in November, after the Springboks won all three July Tests at home with 130 points scored and 49 conceded. Scoring capacity, the piece argues, is the first thing the evidence asks for.

lead.why: The only shortlist item about the Springboks' own Test side, and it looks ahead to the November tour rather than repeating the Esterhuizen or WXV stories.
